title: Latching motor control with emergency-stop interlock
nl_spec: A motor is controlled by momentary Start and Stop pushbuttons and an emergency stop. The motor latches ON when Start is pressed and latches OFF when Stop is pressed; Stop has priority over Start. The emergency stop input EStop is wired normally-closed, so EStop = TRUE means healthy and EStop = FALSE means the emergency stop is ACTIVATED. When the emergency stop is activated it must immediately and unconditionally de-energize the motor, and the motor must not be able to start while it remains activated. Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named motor_interlock with inputs Start, Stop, EStop and output Motor.

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: When the emergency stop is activated (EStop = FALSE), the motor is always off.
Whenever the Stop button is pressed, the motor is off (Stop has priority over Start).

scenarios.description: Start latches motor on, Stop turns it off

notes: Classic seal-in/latch with safety override. Reference uses an ELSIF priority chain so Motor holds its value when no button is pressed.
